recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. Handle any future changes to additional Encounter.basedOn target types under their own Jira decisions, such as FHIR-40634, rather than reopening FHIR-32344.
issue_request: FHIR-32344 was a Published/Persuasive Patient Administration R5 change request asking that Encounter.basedOn allow references to CarePlan, DeviceRequest, and MedicationRequest in addition to the already-supported ServiceRequest.
initial_application: Git commit 19f51434f2a7de172ff4b2cdeb9d7a0087570e93, "FHIR-32344 Encounter.basedOn References", changed the Encounter.basedOn short text from ServiceRequest-specific wording to generic request wording and added CarePlan, DeviceRequest, and MedicationRequest targetProfile entries in source/encounter/structuredefinition-Encounter.xml.
additional_context: Encounter is active in source/fhir.ini, making source/encounter/structuredefinition-Encounter.xml current build source. Later history, especially FHIR-40634 and subsequent immunization resource removal, explains why the current target list is broader than the seed request. The Encounter Event mapping exception is consistent with the current target list. Community searches found no conflicting guidance; Confluence references only confirmed PA meeting context and a later CareTeam discussion that used FHIR-32344 as background.
reconciliation: Published an empty audit commit because the authoritative current source already contains CarePlan, DeviceRequest, and MedicationRequest as Encounter.basedOn target profiles and the relevant mapping-exception source is aligned.

related_jiras.note: Later same element family change that added additional Appointment/Encounter basedOn request target types, explaining why current Encounter.basedOn contains more than FHIR-32344 requested.
PA minutes referenced FHIR-32344 while considering CareTeam support, but that is a separate Encounter relationship and not part of this seed decision.
